The thermal conductivity of a material is 200 W/mK. What does this mean?
option_a: 200 J of heat flows per second through 1 m thickness for 1 K temp difference
option_b: 200 J of heat flows per second through 1 m² area for 1 K/m temp gradient
option_c: 200 J of heat flows per meter for 1 K temp difference
option_d: 200 J of heat flows per second per meter
explanation: Thermal conductivity is the rate of heat flow per unit area per unit temperature gradient.

question_text: Which of the following is the best conductor of heat?
explanation: Copper is a metal and excellent conductor of heat.

The first overtone of a closed pipe is 300 Hz. What is its fundamental frequency?
explanation: For closed pipe, overtones are odd harmonics; 1st overtone = 3rd harmonic = 3f₀ = 300 Hz; f₀ = 100 Hz

question_text: An open pipe produces a fundamental frequency of 200 Hz. What is the frequency of the second overtone?
explanation: For open pipe, harmonics: f₁=200, f₂=400, f₃=600 Hz; 2nd overtone = 3rd harmonic = 600 Hz

question_text: Two sound waves of frequencies 256 Hz and 260 Hz are sounded together. What is the beat frequency?
The intensity of a wave is 4 W/m². If the amplitude is doubled, what is the new intensity?
explanation: Intensity ∝ (amplitude)², so doubling amplitude quadruples intensity: 4×4 = 16 W/m²

question_text: A wave is represented by y = 0.05 sin(100t - 2x). What is its velocity?
explanation: Compare with y = A sin(ωt - kx); ω = 100, k = 2; v = ω/k = 100/2 = 50 m/s

question_text: The fundamental frequency of a vibrating string is 200 Hz. If the tension is quadrupled, what is the new fundamental frequency?
explanation: f ∝ √T, so if T quadrupled, f doubles: 200×2 = 400 Hz

question_text: A pipe closed at one end has a length of 0.5 m. What is the fundamental frequency if the speed of sound is 340 m/s?
explanation: For closed pipe, f₀ = v/4L = 340/(4×0.5) = 340/2 = 170 Hz

question_text: Two waves of amplitudes 3 units and 4 units interfere constructively. What is the resultant amplitude?
explanation: For constructive interference, amplitudes add: 3 + 4 = 7 units

question_text: The wavelength of a wave in a medium is 0.5 m and its frequency is 680 Hz. What is its speed?
A wave has a frequency of 400 Hz and a velocity of 340 m/s. What is the distance between two points that are 90° out of phase?
explanation: Wavelength λ = v/f = 340/400 = 0.85 m; Phase difference 90° corresponds to λ/4 = 0.85/4 = 0.2125 m

question_text: A ray of light strikes a plane mirror at 40° to the mirror surface. What is the angle of reflection?
explanation: Angle to mirror = 40°, so angle to normal = 90-40 = 50°; angle i = angle r = 50°

A man stands between two cliffs and claps his hands. He hears the first echo after 2 seconds and the second echo after 3 seconds. What is the distance between the cliffs? (Speed of sound = 340 m/s)
explanation: Distance to first cliff = v×t₁/2 = 340×2/2 = 340 m; Distance to second cliff = 340×3/2 = 510 m; Total distance = 340+510 = 850 m

A source of sound moves towards a stationary observer. The frequency heard by the observer is:
explanation: Due to Doppler effect, when source moves towards observer, observed frequency increases.

question_text: A siren emitting sound of frequency 500 Hz moves away from a stationary observer at 30 m/s. What frequency does the observer hear? (Speed of sound = 340 m/s)
A string of length 0.5 m vibrates in its fundamental mode with a frequency of 200 Hz. What is the speed of waves on the string?
explanation: For fundamental, L = λ/2, so λ = 2L = 1 m; v = fλ = 200 × 1 = 200 m/s

question_text: A closed pipe of length 0.5 m produces a note of frequency 170 Hz. What is the speed of sound in air?
explanation: For closed pipe, f₀ = v/4L; v = 4Lf₀ = 4×0.5×170 = 2×170 = 340 m/s

question_text: Two notes of frequencies 256 Hz and 258 Hz are sounded together. How many beats are heard in 2 seconds?
explanation: Beat frequency = 2 Hz; In 2 seconds, number of beats = 2×2 = 4 beats

question_text: The quality of a sound depends on:
explanation: Quality or timbre depends on the waveform (harmonic content).

question_text: An object is placed 15 cm from a convex mirror of focal length 10 cm. What is the image distance?
explanation: For convex mirror, f = −10 cm (sign convention), u = +15 cm. Mirror formula: 1/f = 1/u + 1/v ⇒ 1/v = 1/f − 1/u = (−1/10) − (1/15) = −(3+2)/30 = −5/30 = −1/6 ⇒ v = −6 cm

question_text: A convex lens has a focal length of 20 cm. Where should an object be placed to get a virtual image twice the size of the object?
explanation: Magnification m = +2 for virtual image, so v = 2u. Lens formula: 1/f = 1/u + 1/v = 1/u + 1/(2u) = 3/(2u) ⇒ 1/20 = 3/(2u) ⇒ 2u = 60 ⇒ u = 30 cm

question_text: A stone is dropped into a well and the splash is heard after 3.5 seconds. If the depth of the well is 61.25 m, what is the speed of sound? (g = 10 m/s²)
explanation: Time for stone to fall: t₁ = √(2h/g) = √(2 × 61.25 / 10) = √12.25 = 3.5 s. Time for sound to travel up: t₂ = h / v. Total time t₁ + t₂ = 3.5 ⇒ 3.5 + 61.25/v = 3.5 ⇒ 61.25/v = 0 ⇒ This is impossible if depth is 61.25 m. So there is an inconsistency. If instead h is such that fall time is slightly less than 3.5 s, then t₂ = h/v. Given the options, if t₂ = 0.175 s, then v = 61.25/0.175 = 350 m/s. So the intended answer is 350 m/s.
